title: Invert a map: given `Map<String, List<String>>` (department → employee names), create `Map<String, String>` (employee name → department).
shortTitle: Invert a Map<String, List<String>> (department to names) into Map<String, String> (name to department)
keyPoints: Inverting a one-to-many map means flattening each department's list and mapping every name back to its department
Stream entrySet, flatMap to expand the lists into name-department pairs, then collect with toMap
flatMap is the key operation: it turns nested lists into a single flat stream of pairs
If a name appears in two departments, toMap throws unless you supply a merge function
Use Map.entry(name, dept) or AbstractMap.SimpleEntry to create intermediate key-value pairs
For names appearing in multiple departments, invert into Map<String, List<String>> using groupingBy instead

s1_definition.oneliner: Stream entries, flatMap the name lists into name-department pairs, and toMap(name, dept) to invert the map.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **entrySet().stream()** iterates over department-to-names entries.
- **flatMap** expands each department's list of names into individual name-department pairs.
- **toMap(name, department)** builds the inverted map keyed by name.
- If a name appears in two departments, the two-argument toMap throws; add a merge function or use groupingBy.
- **Map.entry(key, value)** creates immutable key-value pairs for the intermediate stream.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya at the National Bank of India has a chart listing who works in each department. She wants the opposite lookup: type a person's name and instantly see their department. So she flips the chart around, turning department-to-names into name-to-department.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Source: Map<String, List<String>>
  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Loans   → [Rajesh, Amit]       │
  │  IT      → [Priya, Kavita]      │
  │  Finance → [Neha]               │
  └─────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       │  flatMap: expand each dept's names
       ▼
  Stream of pairs:
    (Rajesh, Loans), (Amit, Loans),
    (Priya, IT), (Kavita, IT), (Neha, Finance)
       │
       │  toMap(name, dept)
       ▼
  Inverted: Map<String, String>
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │  Rajesh → Loans              │
  │  Amit   → Loans              │
  │  Priya  → IT                 │
  │  Kavita → IT                 │
  │  Neha   → Finance            │
  └──────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Inverting a one-to-many map means taking a map of department-to-names and producing the reverse lookup of name-to-department. Stream the entrySet, and for each entry use flatMap to expand that department's list of names into a stream of name-department pairs. Then collect with toMap keyed by name.

flatMap is the key operation: it flattens nested lists into a single stream of pairs that toMap can rekey. At the National Bank of India, the roster was stored as department-to-names, but the search screen needed the opposite lookup.

The critical point is the uniqueness assumption: this works cleanly only when every name is unique across departments. If a name appears in two departments, toMap throws. Either add a merge function to pick a winner, or invert into Map<String, List<String>> using groupingBy.

Remember one sentence: invert a one-to-many map by flatMapping the lists into name-department pairs and collecting with toMap, and always decide how to handle names appearing in multiple groups.
